title: Relative reductive centre over an arbitrary ring
statement: Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Let $G$ be a reductive $S$-group scheme, with the group-scheme and reductivity conventions of [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization], without a splitness, pinning or maximal-torus hypothesis. Thus $G$ is smooth affine and finitely presented over $S$, with connected reductive geometric fibres. For an $A$-algebra $B$, define $Z_G(B)$ to consist of the $z\in G(B)$ such that for every $B$-algebra $C$ and every $g\in G(C)$ the images of $z$ and $g$ commute. This subgroup functor is represented by a closed subgroup scheme $Z_G\hookrightarrow G$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. It is of multiplicative type of finite presentation: locally for fppf coverings [def-pc-fppf-site], it is isomorphic to $D_U(M)=\operatorname{Spec}_U\mathcal O_U[M]$ for a finitely generated abelian group $M$, with the group-algebra Hopf operations of [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. The morphism $Z_G\to S$ is affine, flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented. For every $A$-algebra $A'$, the canonical map $(Z_G)_{A'}\to Z_{G_{A'}}$ is an isomorphism. Neither Noetherianity or reducedness of $A$ nor smoothness of $Z_G$ is assumed.

source.place: Conrad, Theorem 3.3.4 and proof, printed pp.98--100, with Definition 3.3.3 and the base-change discussion preceding it, pp.97--98. Read online; WANTED local archive as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf. No Stacks tag states this structural group-scheme result.

proof.text: Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}C$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine], $A\to C$ is smooth. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-algebra-finite-type-model] to obtain a subring $A_b\subseteq A$ finitely generated over $\mathbf Z$ and a smooth $A_b$-algebra $C_b$ with $A\otimes_{A_b}C_b\simeq C$. Let $I$ be the set of finitely generated subrings of $A$ containing $A_b$, ordered by inclusion. It is small and directed (adjoin the union of two finite generating sets), and its union is $A$. Its members are nonzero since their unit is that of $A$. Put $S_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ and $X_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A_i\otimes_{A_b}C_b)$. The affine limit formula in [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] identifies $S$ with $\varprojlim_iS_i$. The $S_i$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], and their transition maps are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. Each $X_i/S_i$ is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2) and the affine smoothness equivalence just cited.

source.place: Tag 00TP, lemma-finite-presentation-fs-Noetherian; affine passage by 01V6/02H6, limits by 01YW, smooth base change by 02H2.

proof.text: Descend the group operations, not just the underlying scheme. The coordinate algebras of $X_i$, $X_i\times_{S_i}X_i$ and $X_i^3$ are finitely presented: use [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-product-finitely-presented-algebras] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Such affine schemes are locally of finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). By clause (2) of [thm-pd-spreading-out], the multiplication $G\times_SG\to G$, inverse $G\to G$ and identity $S\to G$ descend to one common index $i$. Clause (3) descends the associativity equality on $X_i^3$, the two unit equalities on $X_i$, and the two inverse equalities on $X_i$. There are only finitely many equalities, so directedness gives one index where all hold. Thus $X_i$ is a smooth affine finitely presented group $G_i$, and its base change is isomorphic to $G$ as a group. Later models are obtained by base change, with the same properties; finite presentation persists by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3).

source.place: Tag 01ZM, lemma-descend-finite-presentation, clauses (2),(3), applied to the three operations and the finite group-diagram equalities.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-reductivity-eventual-ring-colimit] to this directed system and the smooth affine finitely presented group $G_i$. Its limit is the given reductive $G$, so for some later index the group $G_0$ is reductive over the entire $\operatorname{Spec}A_0$, not merely over points hit by $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Here $A_0\subseteq A$ is nonzero and finitely generated over $\mathbf Z$. The ring $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian: a nonzero ideal has a least positive element, and division with remainder proves that element generates the ideal; the zero ideal is generated by zero. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $A_0$ Noetherian. We have obtained a reductive Noetherian model $G_0$ with a specified group isomorphism $(G_0)_A\simeq G$, without choosing a torus or pinning.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.11 and proof, printed pp.88--89; Noetherian permanence is Stacks Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-reductive-centre-weight-kernel] over $A_0$. Its hypotheses hold: $A_0$ is nonzero Noetherian, and $G_0$ is smooth affine of finite type with connected reductive geometric fibres. It gives a closed centre $Z_0\hookrightarrow G_0$, flat over $A_0$, locally of the form $D_U(N)$ for finitely generated abelian $N$, and compatible with arbitrary base change. Also $Z_0$ is affine and finitely presented over $A_0$: write $G_0=\operatorname{Spec}C_0$; the affine characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion] writes $Z_0=\operatorname{Spec}(C_0/J)$. A finite set of algebra generators of $C_0$ maps to generators of $C_0/J$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] to this finite-type $A_0$-algebra. Its spectrum is locally of finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and then of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). The structural map is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine].

source.place: Theorem 3.3.4, centre portion of the proof, printed pp.98--99; finite presentation from Stacks Tag 00FP, lemma-Noetherian-finite-type-is-finite-presentation, and Tag 01TP.

proof.text: Set $Z=Z_0\times_{A_0}A$ and use $(G_0)_A\simeq G$ for its inclusion. The arbitrary-base-change clause of [lem-sfb-relative-reductive-centre-weight-kernel], applied to $A_0\to A$, says exactly that this represents the functor $Z_G$ of the statement on every $A$-algebra. Its inclusion is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Its structural map is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change] and finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). If $Z_0=\operatorname{Spec}Q_0$, then [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] gives $Z=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_{A_0}Q_0)$, so [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] also gives the required affineness over $S$. All group operations are the base changes of those of $Z_0$.

source.place: Theorem 3.3.4, printed pp.98--99; arbitrary base change of the centre as already stated by the cited Noetherian theorem; Stacks Tags 01U9 and 01TS.

proof.text: Take an fppf cover $\{U_j\to\operatorname{Spec}A_0\}$ on which $Z_0$ is $D_{U_j}(N_j)$, as supplied by [lem-sfb-relative-reductive-centre-weight-kernel]. Pulling it back to $S$ gives an fppf cover by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change]. On an affine chart $U_j=\operatorname{Spec}R$, base change to $\operatorname{Spec}R\prime$ carries $R[N_j]$ to $R\prime[N_j]$: the maps $r\prime\otimes\sum a_n e_n\mapsto\sum r\prime a_n e_n$ and $\sum b_n e_n\mapsto\sum b_n\otimes e_n$ are inverse. They preserve multiplication, coproduct, counit and antipode on each basis element by [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]; [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies the corresponding group schemes. These formulas restrict to the same formulas on smaller affine charts, so give the same identification over a general $U_j$. Hence $Z$ is fppf locally $D(N_j)$ with the same finitely generated character groups. Torsion in $N_j$ has not been removed.

source.place: Definition 3.3.3 and Theorem 3.3.4, printed pp.98--99; Appendix B.1, printed p.280; Stacks Tag 021O, lemma-fppf, part (3).

proof.text: Finally let $A\to A\prime$ be arbitrary. Apply the arbitrary-base-change assertion of [lem-sfb-relative-reductive-centre-weight-kernel] directly to the composite $A_0\to A\prime$. Both $(Z_G)_{A\prime}$ and $Z_{G_{A\prime}}$ identify with $(Z_0)_{A\prime}$ as subgroup functors of $(G_0)_{A\prime}$. Explicitly, on every $A\prime$-algebra $B$, both consist of precisely those $z\in G_0(B)$ commuting with every $g\in G_0(C)$ for every $B$-algebra $C$; the $B$-algebras in the two descriptions are identical. The comparison therefore sends a point to that same point of $G_0(B)$ and is bijective naturally in $B$. These representable functors give the canonical group-scheme isomorphism, and its naturality also proves compatibility with successive base changes. If $A\prime$ is the zero ring, both schemes are empty over the empty base and the same assertion holds. No step required $A$ or $A\prime$ to be reduced or Noetherian, or $Z$ to be smooth.
